We demonstrate that complex ellipsoids in $\mathbb{C}^n$ are uniquely characterized by specific geometric attributes related to their complex sections, properties that also apply to a broader category of convex bodies within this context. Additionally, we establish an existence theorem regarding polyhedra in $\mathbb{C}^n$ defined by specified complex support values.

The rapid advancement of data collection and analysis technologies has generated a paradoxical situation: while these capabilities offer significant benefits, they also trigger widespread anxiety and distrust among the general public. To address this, we introduce a novel visualization tool designed to help individuals comprehend the underlying mechanisms of data collection. By enabling users to explore the system as a dynamic, interactive model, the tool fosters a deeper understanding of how personal information is gathered and utilized. We posit that this enhanced understanding can empower individuals to make more informed decisions regarding their data privacy.

Faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling enables the transmission of data at a rate surpassing the Nyquist limit by deliberately inducing inter-symbol interference (ISI). However, this interference renders the received signal non-linear and time-varying, complicating the design of optimal receivers. This study introduces a generalized framework for FTN signaling that encompasses both linear and non-linear receiver architectures. We demonstrate that the ideal non-linear structure for the receiver is a neural network, and we propose a method to train this network using a novel, efficient algorithm. Simulation outcomes indicate that the proposed neural network-based non-linear receiver achieves superior performance compared to conventional linear FTN receivers.

This work establishes that a complete atomic lattice effect algebra is precisely equivalent to a directed, upper-continuous, algebraic distributive lattice. As a result, we obtain an extension of the Birkhoff dual representation theorem for these algebras, accompanied by a characterization of the specific subset of representable algebras.

This paper introduces SaliencyMix, a data augmentation technique that leverages the saliency maps of two images to create a new one. The approach involves blending the saliency maps of two source images to determine a composite image. The resulting augmented samples have been shown to improve the performance of various image classification models on the CIFAR-100 dataset. The source code for the proposed method is available at https://github.com/abdulrahmanmohamed/SaliencyMix.

We construct quantum algebras as convolution algebras formed by bi-invariant functions defined on the group $G_n(\mathbb{Z}_p)$, consisting of units within the special $p$-adic matrix algebra. Furthermore, we establish that these algebras are semisim for the case where $p$ is an odd prime.

Cosmic shear surveys are frequently analyzed by assuming that the shapes of individual galaxies are uncorrelated, a premise that fails to account for intrinsic alignments (IA) between neighbors. This study examines how such intrinsic shape correlations influence the accuracy of cosmological parameter estimation. We introduce a novel method to model these correlations by utilizing the covariance matrix of IA fields, which we demonstrate can be effectively captured through a Gaussian process. We then quantify the resulting bias in cosmological parameters by comparing results derived from the Gaussian process against those from the standard uncorrelated assumption. Our findings indicate that while the impact of intrinsic shape correlations is negligible for the COSMOS and DES datasets, it becomes significant for the LSST and Euclid surveys. Furthermore, we observe that the magnitude of this effect is closely tied to the specific IA model employed.

Soft-deformable particle systems are widely used to model various soft matter, including biological tissues, colloids, and polymers. While these systems are known to exhibit shear banding under large strains, the conditions governing this localization remain unclear. This study investigates the onset of shear banding in two-dimensional systems of soft-deformable particles using shear tests. We demonstrate that for large strains, shear stress and mechanical energy decay exponentially with strain, a behavior driven by the softness of the interparticle potential. Consequently, shear banding emerges when the system size falls below a critical threshold, a condition that can be predicted using a simplified one-dimensional model.

Machine learning force fields (MLFFs) have recently become a powerful tool for investigating the atomic-scale dynamics of nanomaterials. This study introduces an MLFF designed for gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) that accurately reproduces the energy, stress, and interatomic potentials of bulk gold across various strain levels. The training dataset comprises 1,000 configurations derived from molecular dynamics simulations of bulk gold, supplemented by 100 additional configurations generated through ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. Utilizing the active learning framework of the atomic environment descriptor, the model was iteratively refined by selecting the most informative configurations for retraining. Consequently, the resulting MLFF achieves a mean absolute error of 0.01 eV/atom in predicting energies and 0.01 eV/Å in predicting forces. When applied to AuNPs with diameters ranging from 2 to 10 nm, the MLFF successfully simulates their structural evolution and surface reconstruction. Furthermore, the model's performance was validated against experimental data, demonstrating its reliability in analyzing the dynamics of gold nanoparticles.

This study investigates the minimal extension of the Standard Model required to resolve the generation count problem. We introduce a hypothesis positing that the three fermion families possess a shared origin, linked by a non-standard gauge symmetry. This study introduces $(h; q)$-Genocchi numbers and polynomials within the framework of $q$-Bernstein polynomials. We provide explicit expressions for these numbers and polynomials using $q$-Bernstein polynomials in this context. Additionally, we investigate the relationship between the Stirling numbers of the second kind and the $q$-Bernstein polynomials, alongside an analysis of the zeros found in $(h; q)$-Genocchi polynomials.

Randomized experiments are widely regarded as the gold standard for estimating causal effects, yet their short-term nature often limits their ability to accurately measure long-term treatment impacts. To address this, we introduce a novel framework for estimating long-term effects that integrates randomized experiments with observational data. This approach leverages the randomization inherent in experiments to establish a causal bridge connecting the short-term effects observed in trials to the long-term outcomes derived from observational records. We demonstrate that this framework is both necessary and sufficient, and we develop a specific model satisfying these conditions. Furthermore, we propose a method to estimate long-term treatment effects that utilizes data from both sources, proving that our estimator is consistent and asymptotically normal. Empirical evaluations using both synthetic datasets and real-world data confirm that our method achieves superior accuracy compared to existing techniques.

Case-control studies are frequently utilized to investigate rare diseases, yet they are susceptible to recall bias, which can compromise the accuracy of exposure data. This paper introduces a novel approach to mitigate such bias by leveraging information from external sources. The method employs a Bayesian framework to integrate external data, which is assumed to be independent of the study's outcome, with the primary dataset. Specifically, we model the external data using a logistic regression framework. The proposed approach is demonstrated through an application to a cohort examining the link between diabetes and caesarean section rates, incorporating relevant external data. The study also outlines a diagnostic framework for assessing the impact of external data and illustrates how the method can be adapted to address missing data challenges.

Autoencoders (AEs) are widely utilized for generating data and modeling its distribution. However, their ability to capture the full data distribution is constrained by the limited capacity of their latent space. Conversely, normalizing flows offer a solution by establishing a closed-form density estimation through a sequence of invertible transformations. This paper introduces Autoencoder with Flows (AEF), a hybrid approach that integrates a standard AEs with normalizing flows. By concatenating flows to the A's bottleneck, AEF expands the latent space's capacity, enabling a more expressive representation. We evaluate this method on both synthetic datasets and real-world image data, comparing it against Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and other latent normalizing flows. The results demonstrate that the proposed AEF architecture achieves superior performance in both likelihood estimation and image synthesis quality.

Urban sensing research has recently gained significant traction, driven by the widespread availability of diverse urban data. While numerous studies have focused on mining patterns within this data, they typically overlook the interconnections between different data sources. This paper introduces the concept of Correlated Attribute Patterns (CAP) to address CAP mining, a task designed to uncover attribute patterns across multiple data sources that exhibit high confidence and support. We establish the formal definition of CAP mining, identify its computational challenges, and subsequently propose the CorPaMiner algorithm to efficiently solve this problem. Experimental results using real-world datasets demonstrate that the CorPaMiner algorithm is both effective and scalable.

This study introduces a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) approach for solving coupled reaction-diffusion equations and the generalized Stokes equations. The proposed method employs a face variable as the local interface trace, with a polynomial approximation of degree $k+1$ ($k \geq 0$) on each element, while globally solving a reduced system using a single degree ($k$) polynomial on each element. Theoretical analysis confirms that the method achieves optimal convergence rates for both approximations. Numerical experiments validate these theoretical findings and demonstrate the method's efficiency.

Sensitivity analysis is designed to evaluate how missing data mechanisms might influence the findings of a study. In scenarios where outcome data are missing, researchers often employ Sensitivity Analysis (SA) to test the robustness of conclusions against various plausible assumptions regarding unobserved data. A prevalent method within this framework is Pattern Mixing (PM), which models missingness as a latent indicator variable. However, the latent indicator variable in PM is not directly observable, making it challenging to incorporate external knowledge about the missingness mechanism. To address this limitation, we introduce a modified PM model that integrates external information by defining the latent indicator variable as a function of external covariates. We demonstrate the utility of this approach through an analysis of data from the Women's Health Initiative study, which examined the effects of hormone replacement therapy on cholesterol levels in the presence of missing data.

In the context of analyzing gene expression data from crossover trials that suffer from missing responses, the mixed-effects model with maximum likelihood estimation is typically preferred. However, when the missing data mechanism is not ignorable, maximum likelihood analysis becomes invalid. This study introduces a Bayesian framework for gene expression analysis that accommodates non-ignorable missingness, utilizing a model-based imputation strategy. Specifically, we employ a joint model combining a primary linear mixed-effects model for observed responses with a secondary model for missing ones; the latter incorporates a Tobit structure to address potential limits of detection. Furthermore, we integrate prior distributions for the correlation parameters linking the two models to explicitly account for the non-ignorable nature of the missing data. The proposed methodology is demonstrated through an application to a dataset from a proteomics study.

This paper introduces a category-theoretic definition for the $A_n$ structure, which is a weak generalization of $A_\infty$ algebras. We establish that the $A_n$ structure on a category corresponds to a monad within a category of categories. Furthermore, we define a 2-category wherein the objects are categories equipped with $A_n$ structures, and the morphisms are functors acting as morphisms of these structures. We demonstrate that this category admits a monadic structure, with the associated monad's objects being cocommutative bimonads defined over the 2-category of categories.

DRAM is a widely adopted memory technology, yet its inherent limitations in programmability and flexibility have hindered its potential. To address this, DRAM has recently incorporated internal programmable timings, offering a promising avenue for boosting both performance and reliability. In this study, we introduce a novel DRAM-based memory system that leverages these internal timing controls to achieve a new class of DRAM primitives. These primitives facilitate the creation of a new memory architecture termed "Programmatic DRAM" (PDRAM). PDRAM supports a wide array of applications, including a new approach to data protection called "Data Shielding," which aims to prevent data leakage by rendering sensitive information unreadable to unauthorized parties. Experimental results indicate that Data Shielding can effectively stop data exfiltration via DRAM side-channel attacks, achieving a performance overhead of merely 1.4%. Furthermore, we demonstrate that PDRAM can be utilized to construct a new type of memory primitive known as "Programmable DRAM Random Number Generator" (PDRNG). PDRNG generates cryptographically secure random numbers with a performance impact of only 1.8%.

Network Functions Virtualization (NFV) represents a novel approach to network operation that enables the deployment of network functions as software on standard off-the-shelf servers. This shift allows for the flexible and efficient allocation of resources, facilitating the rapid provisioning of network services. However, the NFV paradigm has also introduced significant challenges, particularly in the area of security. This paper examines the security landscape of NFV, identifying key issues and potential solutions, while also highlighting the interplay between NFV and Software-Defined Networking (SDN).

This work introduces a fault-tolerant quantum architecture utilizing a surface code enhanced with multi-qubit gates, which significantly lowers the count of physical qubits and physical operations required for logical operations. The design employs a hybrid approach combining local interactions across the entire system with non-local operations facilitated by a network of quantum repeaters. Multi-qubit gates are implemented through the creation of entangled states between distant qubits, which are then distributed via the aforementioned repeater network. The analysis demonstrates that this architecture substantially reduces the overhead associated with fault-tolerant quantum computing, particularly in terms of physical qubit requirements and gate operations.

OPUS (Optimization and Parameter Uncertainty Solving) is a modular framework designed to facilitate the integration of analysis and simulation codes within the OPAL environment. It enables the execution of optimization and probabilistic assessments, including sensitivity analysis, by managing the orchestration of multiple codes, handling input and output data, and performing post-processing. Built on a modular architecture, OPUS accommodates a wide range of tools, from deterministic solvers like ANSYS and COMSOL to uncertainty quantification packages such as UQlab and DAKOTA. The system's flexibility allows users to construct complex workflows, such as nested Monte Carlo simulations, and offers a graphical interface for defining these processes.

Digital Game-Based Learning (DGBL) has become a vital component of modern education, offering an engaging and effective method to enhance student experience. This paper introduces a DGBL prototype designed to support undergraduate engineering education. The system's architecture is built on the Unity game engine, which facilitates the development of interactive, 3D environments. The research evaluates the system's impact on student learning outcomes, specifically targeting the field of Computer Engineering. Additionally, the study examines the system's effectiveness in fostering student engagement.

Molecular oxygen (O2) and ozone (O3) are essential for life on Earth, with O2 originating from photosynthesis and O3 forming from O2 via solar UV radiation. Consequently, O2 and O3 levels are not independent; they are linked through both biological and chemical processes. This study examines the relationship between O2 and O3 by analyzing a dataset of 1,000 simulated scenarios, each containing two time series with varying lengths and autocorrelation structures. We employ a Bayesian framework to model the joint distribution of these series, accounting for their interdependence and internal dynamics. We find that the posterior distribution of the O2-O3 relationship is highly sensitive to the choice of prior, suggesting that the observed correlation may be spurious. We also demonstrate that the method is robust to measurement noise and that the O2-O3 relationship can be estimated accurately even with limited data. Finally, we discuss the implications of our findings for understanding the role of O2 and O3 in the biosphere.

We introduce a three-dimensional lattice model featuring a robust three-dimensional crosscurrent that maintains its current despite the presence of two types of point defects. This current is protected topologically by a single non-trivial tricritical invariant, which is a homotopy class of a three-dimensional mapping from the bulk to a target space. This invariant is constructed from a set of three critical points in the bulk, each corresponding to a Dirac point. The crosscurrent proves to be stable against the introduction of a single impurity. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the system's bulk properties can be characterized through a three-dimensional generalization of the Berry connection and curvature.

Multilingual neural machine translation (NMT) systems have demonstrated the ability to enhance translation quality for low-resource languages by leveraging data from linguistically related languages. This study introduces a new NMT system trained on 112 languages, including the 10 languages of the WMT 2022 task, and presents a comprehensive evaluation of the system's performance across 10 language pairs against the NLLB 2022 model. The analysis reveals that NLLB 2022 achieves superior results on most language pairs, though it fails to outperform the NLLB 2022 model on specific pairs. To address this, we conducted a targeted investigation into the NLLB 2022 model's performance on these challenging pairs, examining the influence of language similarity, available training data, and the model's internal representations. The findings indicate that the NLLB 2022 model struggles with these pairs primarily due to a lack of robust multilingual representations for the involved languages. Consequently, we propose a new training strategy that improves NLLB 2022's performance on these pairs by strengthening its multilingual representations.

This study examines the formation of ion-acoustic waves in a dusty plasma environment consisting of non-thermal, non-Maxwellian electrons and positrons, alongside positively charged dust grains and fixed ions. By employing a kinetic approach, we derive a kinetic model for these waves, which is subsequently analyzed using a fluid model to determine the non-thermal parameters governing both frameworks. The analysis reveals that the derived kinetic and fluid models yield identical results when applied within the fluid model's domain.

Recent developments in dense retrieval have been driven by pre-trained language models, which are typically trained on extensive datasets. However, these models often fail to capture the specific nuances required for specialized domains. To address this, we introduce a two-stage pre-training approach for domain-specific dense retrieval. In the initial stage, a model is pre-trained on a large corpus of domain-specific documents using a masked language modeling task. In the subsequent stage, a second model is trained on a dataset of document pairs, utilizing the representations from the first stage to optimize retrieval performance. We evaluate this method on two datasets: the MS-MARCO passage retrieval benchmark and a new, large-scale dataset comprising 1.2 million pairs of medical questions and abstracts. Our results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods in both the MS-MARCO and medical domains.

Multimodal learning (MML) seeks to integrate information from diverse sources, such as text and images, to enhance the performance of machine learning models. A primary challenge in MML is the inherent heterogeneity among these varied data types. While numerous methods have been developed to address this, many fail to fully exploit the rich semantic relationships between modalities. This paper introduces a new approach called the Multimodal Graph Attention Network (MuGAT), which leverages a multimodal graph to capture semantic interconnections between modalities and employs a graph attention mechanism to learn a unified embedding space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of MuGAT through experiments on the Microsoft COCO dataset, where it outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in object captioning and visual question answering.

We investigate the relativistic quantum dynamics of massless fermions within a finite volume, focusing on the vector and axial vector two-point correlation functions. By employing the framework of the spectral density operator, we establish a relationship linking these correlation functions to the spectrum of the massless Dirac operator. We demonstrate that the vector two-point correlation function vanishes at leading order in the chiral limit, whereas the axial vector correlation function exhibits a non-vanishing component at leading order that is independent of volume.

This study introduces a novel, end-to-end, spoken command recognition system utilizing a tensor-train network. The proposed architecture employs a single, unified tensor-train structure to simultaneously process the entire spoken command, thereby eliminating the need for separate classification or localization modules. This approach effectively addresses the inherent challenges of spoken command recognition, specifically the limited dataset size and the high variability in command duration. The model's efficacy is validated through experiments on the OpenAI/Google OpenSpeech 1000 command dataset, where it achieved a 90.4% accuracy rate.

Quantum-jump unravelings are widely used for open quantum systems, yet they fail to exist in certain scenarios. This study demonstrates that such unavailable unravelings can be recovered by embedding the system into a larger framework that includes an auxiliary component. The proposed approach is validated through numerical simulations of a quantum-jump unraveling for a specific open system originally lacking one.

The optical characteristics of nanoparticles are determined by their size and morphology, which in turn dictate how they absorb light within solar cells. This study investigates how the shape of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) influences the performance of silicon hetero-junction solar cells (c-Si). We compared spherical AuNPs with those of irregular shapes, analyzing their impact on light absorption and overall device efficiency. The results demonstrate that irregularly shaped AuNPs significantly enhance light capture in thin-film c-Si compared to their spherical counterparts. Furthermore, we examined the influence of AuNP concentration on cell performance, observing that an optimal concentration of 0.5% yields the highest efficiency.

We introduce a novel framework for defining first-order logic with counting augmented by a specific set of polynomial-time functions. This approach, inspired by the concept of fixed points, draws a parallel to the role of least fixed points in logic. We demonstrate that the specific polynomial-time functions selected to enrich the logic precisely characterize the class of deterministic polynomial-time logic programs. Furthermore, we establish a connection between these logical programs and the broader deterministic polynomial-time fixed-point logic framework.

LSTMs are widely employed for sequence prediction, yet they often demand substantial memory and training time. This paper introduces a novel, memory-efficient LSTM framework designed to reduce complexity without sacrificing accuracy. The approach utilizes a hierarchical structure that integrates a compact, low-parameter model with a larger, high-parameter model. The system operates in two phases: first, a small model is trained on a subset of data to generate initial predictions; second, if these predictions fall below a specific accuracy threshold, the data is re-sampled, and the larger model is trained on this refined subset to update or replace the existing models. Theoretically, this method is proven to converge toward a set of optimal models. Empirical evaluations across various datasets demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves performance comparable to standard LSTMs while significantly lowering computational requirements.

The Multi-purpose Autonomous Vehicle Link (MAVLIC) communication protocol is widely utilized in autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs). However, the protocol's inherent design exposes it to significant security threats, including denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, authentication bypasses, and command injection. This study examines the security properties of MAVLCN by analyzing its underlying mechanisms and identifying specific vulnerabilities. We present a comprehensive framework for assessing these risks, which categorizes potential attack vectors into three primary types: authentication breaches, command injection, and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. Furthermore, we detail the specific implementation of these threats and provide a comprehensive analysis of their impacts.

The rise of large-scale distributed systems has made it crucial to understand network characteristics like latency, bandwidth, and reliability. This study introduces a novel, high-performance, and scalable framework designed to automatically gather these traits. The solution utilizes a distributed architecture that leverages the target environment's existing resources to perform measurements, while its internal components are designed for scalability and efficiency. The methodology is evaluated through a series of experiments that demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately and efficiently computing network metrics.

This study examines a specific class of self-dual solutions to vacuum Maxwell equations formulated in terms of twistor theory. By applying a generalized Penrose transform, we derive the corresponding self-dual Maxwell spacetime solutions. Furthermore, we establish a relationship between these electromagnetic configurations and specific Einstein vacuum solutions, effectively extending the concept of double self-duality within Maxwell-Edwards theory.

This paper details the design and implementation of a muon detector intended to examine voids within the 1,000-ton concrete foundation of the Large Hadron Collider. Parsing Expression Grammars (PEGs) are a popular alternative to context-free grammars, distinguished by their unambiguous, left-to-right, and deterministic nature. While PEGs support recursive structures and are utilized in diverse applications like data formats and search engines, this paper introduces ordered choice as a new PEG construct. This feature enables the definition of alternative options for a specific position, selecting the first option that successfully parses the input. We demonstrate that this enhancement expands PEG's expressive power, allowing for a more comprehensive representation of various data types.

This study examines the Cherenkov radiation of a scalar field by a heavy particle within a thermal bath, employing the thermal effective action to evaluate the rate. We demonstrate that, at sufficiently high temperatures, the rate exhibits a linear temperature dependence, consistent with findings for light particles. Furthermore, we identify that the rate is modulated by the Cherenkov mechanism's threshold, which is determined by the mass of the heavy particle and the temperature.

Recent research indicates that the human brain encodes linguistic information through neural responses that mirror the underlying structure of language. This study investigates how well various modeling approaches can capture these neural representations by fitting electroencephalogram (EEG) data using three distinct methods: a cutting-edge neural language model, a probabilistic category model, and a traditional psycholinguistic model. The results demonstrate that predictability scores derived from the advanced neural language model are superior to those from the simpler category model and the psycholinguistic approach in accounting for the observed EEG patterns. Furthermore, the study reveals that neural representations are more strongly correlated with the semantic category of words than with their specific meanings.

Estimating the 3D pose of objects from a single viewpoint is a critical challenge in computer vision, with significant applications in robotics, augmented reality, and autonomous driving. While current state-of-the-art methods typically depend on 3D-labeled data from controlled environments, they often fail to generalize to real-world scenarios. To address this, we introduce a new approach for single-view 3D object pose estimation that leverages vast collections of unstructured real-world videos. Our method utilizes a novel 3D pose regression framework that integrates a 3D-aware attention mechanism with a 3D-aware contrastive learning strategy. This design enables the model to learn robust 3D object representations and effectively handle diverse object categories. Furthermore, we introduce a new benchmark dataset called OVPose, comprising 1.2 million videos of 100 object categories captured by consumer cameras. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods on both OVPose and the standard OC3D dataset.

Andreev bound states (ABS) within semiconductor-superconductor heterostructures are promising for creating hybrid qubits, yet their coupling mechanisms in multi-wire systems remain poorly understood. This study investigates the interaction between ABS in two parallel quantum wires, revealing that their coupling is mediated by both proximity effects and exchange interactions. We demonstrate that the exchange coupling facilitates non-local spin dynamics, enabling the generation of non-local spin currents and entangled spin states across the two wires. Furthermore, we show that ABS can enhance the efficiency of these exchange-coupled spin dynamics. These findings suggest that ABS can be harnessed to engineer complex hybrid systems capable of hosting both topological and non-topological qubits.

Magnetic reconnection is a primary mechanism for energizing particles within astrophysical plasmas. This study examines particle acceleration driven by reconnection in a magnetized plasma, specifically focusing on the relativistic regime. We analyze the electron distribution function resulting from reconnection in a two-dimensional relativistic plasma, utilizing a one-dimensional kinetic model. The study demonstrates that electrons gain energy through both direct processes and indirect mechanisms. Furthermore, we observe that the resulting distribution functions exhibit a power-law tail, a feature consistent with observations of solar flares and gamma-ray bursts.

This study examines the one-loop corrections to the Higgsstrahlung process ($e^+e^- \to ZH$) within a model featuring an extended scalar sector, specifically a two-Higgs-doublet model with a triplet field. We calculate the shifts in the longitudinal and transverse cross-sections, incorporating all relevant one-loop contributions. Our results demonstrate that neglecting these effects leads to inaccuracies in the predicted values of the cross-sections.

This paper investigates the subgradient of the joint numerical radius within multilinear mappings. We introduce a characterization of its subgradient that mirrors the well-established definition for the joint numerical radius of a matrix. Furthermore, our findings establish a criterion for when joint numerical radius is differentiable. As a direct consequence, we derive a formula for its derivative.

Deep learning has become a cornerstone of the AI field, with its frameworks now widely adopted across numerous domains. However, the integration of deep learning into artificial intelligence has introduced a new class of privacy and security challenges, including data poisoning, model inversion, and membership inference attacks. This study examines these specific vulnerabilities within the context of financial trading data and corresponding deep learning architectures. We begin by evaluating the susceptibility of various deep learning models to data poisoning when trained on financial datasets. Subsequently, we assess the models' resistance against both membership inference attacks and adversarial attacks. Our findings indicate that while financial data presents a significant challenge to deep learning, it remains vulnerable to privacy and security threats.

This study examines the eigensystem associated with multivariate second-order stochastic mappings, demonstrating that these mappings exhibit a reproducing kernel Hilbert space structure. We establish that these eigenvectors function as principal components of covariance-like matrices, which are derived from the spectral density of the underlying processes. We further analyze the eigensystems of the second-order Stochastic Partial Analysis (SPAs) and Principal Component Analysis (PCAs) within the context of multivariate settings. We demonstrate that these eigensystems can be expressed as solutions to the corresponding integral equations, and we show that the eigenvectors can be expressed as solutions to the corresponding integral equations, which are derived from the spectral density of the underlying processes. This study introduces a new ignition model for high-pressure hydrogen-oxygen mixtures, which integrates the effects of external energy sources, pressure, and the quantity of seed electrons. The proposed approach employs a simplified, two-step mechanism to describe ignition and combustion. A novel criterion is established to determine the conditions under which external energy sources can trigger ignition. The model's predictions are validated against experimental data from shock tubes and spark-ignited internal combustion chambers. The findings indicate that the model accurately forecasts ignition delay times and combustion pressures across a wide range of conditions, including various temperatures, pressures, and ignition methods. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that seed electrons are critical for initiating combustion in these H₂–O₂ mixtures.

Accurate image segmentation is essential for numerous applications, including medical image analysis and autonomous driving. While Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have achieved remarkable success in this field, they often struggle with precise boundary detection. To address this limitation, we introduce a Boundary-Aware Segmentation Network (BASNet) designed to enhance segmentation accuracy. BASNet integrates three core components: a feature pyramid network, a boundary-aware module, and a boundary-aware loss function. The feature pyramid network generates a multi-scale feature map to capture details at varying resolutions. The boundary-aware module then utilizes these multi-scale features to isolate object boundaries. Finally, the boundary-aware loss function optimizes the network by emphasizing the correct classification of boundary pixels. Experiments conducted on the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset demonstrate that BASNet achieves state-of-the-art results, surpassing existing methods.

Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication significantly enhances the situational awareness of Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) by facilitating the exchange of critical data regarding their own state and that of surrounding entities. This paper introduces a novel framework for detecting anomalies within CA velocity profiles, leveraging the ability to utilize velocity data from neighboring vehicles to identify irregularities. The approach employs a machine learning-based intrusion detection system designed to recognize anomalous velocity patterns. Furthermore, the study examines the efficacy of machine learning algorithms for anomaly detection under various traffic conditions and data availability scenarios. Finally, the proposed system is evaluated against a real-world dataset to demonstrate its performance.

This study examines the collective behavior of active particles confined within a two-dimensional channel, distinguishing between a "weakly active" population that undergoes Brownian motion and an "strongly active" group driven by self-propulsion. We analyze how the density, flow velocity, and particle structure evolve as the strength of self-propulsion increases, alongside variations in particle concentration and channel dimensions. Our findings reveal that weakly active particles exhibit a non-monotonic density profile near the walls, transitioning from a depletion layer to an accumulation layer as activity rises. Furthermore, we observe that the flow field of self-propelled particles displays a non-monotonic response to the strength of self-propulsion, shifting from a depletion to an accumulation of particles in the immediate vicinity of the boundary.

Electronic states within plasmas are conventionally modeled as the superposition of a neutral atom and a free electron. Siegert states, which we introduce here, are constructed using a scattering framework, treating the free electron and neutral atom as scattering entities. We demonstrate that these two methodologies are fundamentally linked, with Siegert states emerging as corrections to the standard description. This relationship is established by deriving a specific connection between the wave functions and transition matrix elements of the scattering approach and those of the asymptotic method. Our findings are substantiated through calculations of the photoionization cross section for hydrogen plasmas.

Solar flares are characterized by the sudden release of magnetic energy, which triggers a range of dynamic phenomena, including the "Moreton-Bright" transient (MBT). These events are marked by a rapid increase in emission intensity and velocity within the He II 1640 Å line, occurring roughly 10 to 30 seconds after the initial onset of a flare. This study examines the characteristics of the MBT using data from the Solar Dynamics Observatory's Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (SDO/AIA). The analysis reveals that the MBT is a localized phenomenon, with a typical spatial extent of approximately 10,000 kilometers. The observed intensity variations in the He II 1640 Å line occur with a periodicity of about 10 seconds, a pattern that correlates with the magnetic reconnection process. Furthermore, the MBT is consistently observed in the vicinity of the flare's footpoints, suggesting that the observed behavior is driven by the release of magnetic energy during the flare event.

By analyzing the static quark-antiquark potential, we find that the $\theta$-term induces a $\theta$-dependent shift in the interquark potential's minimum separation, $r_{\rm min}$. This study examines how the critical angle for ion-beam irradiation varies with incident angle, ion species, energy, and target material. Utilizing molecular dynamics simulations, we modeled the irradiation of amorphous silica targets using helium, neon, argon, and krypton ions at energies of 10, 20, 30, 50, and 100 keV. We determined the critical angle by monitoring the evolution of the amorphous fraction in relation to the incident angle. Our findings indicate that the critical angle increases with higher ion energy and changes based on the ion species, but remains unaffected by the target material. Furthermore, we observed that the critical angle is lower for targets with a higher amorphous fraction.

Source code anti-plagiarism systems utilize a combination of cryptography and data structures to detect unauthorized modifications in programs. This paper introduces a novel approach that integrates an efficient hash function with a binary tree to achieve a time complexity of O(log n) for both fingerprinting and matching processes. The study details the specific cryptographic methods employed and provides a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance. Furthermore, it outlines the advantages of the proposed system and benchmarks its results against existing anti-plagiarism solutions.
We establish the absence of solutions for the equation $f^\ast g = 1$ within the domain of Dirichlet series featuring polynomial coefficient growth.

We establish a finitely generated subgroup of $SU(3,\mathbb{Z}[\xi_{13}])$, where $\mathbb{Z}[\xi_{13}]$ denotes the Eisenstein integer ring over $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_{13}]$, that possesses a $(k,r)$-approximate subgroup containing at least $k^9$ elements for every $r > 0$. This finding confirms that the answer to a question originally posed by G. A. Bobylev and A. A. Kuznetsov in 2009 is affirmative.

We introduce a new method for estimating log-concave densities through a log-constrained regression framework. This approach is particularly effective for parametric log-concave inference, where the target density is defined by a finite set of parameters. By applying this technique to data drawn from a mixture of log-concave distributions, we demonstrate that the resulting estimator achieves asymptotic normality and derives an explicit expression for its asymptotic variance. Furthermore, we utilize this methodology to perform nonparametric hypothesis testing, specifically for assessing equality between two log-concave densities. Simulations are provided to evaluate the performance of our proposed tests.

This study introduces a modified Wang-Landau algorithm designed to efficiently sample static configurations in granular systems, specifically those involving frictionless spheres. By employing a biasing factor that adjusts based on the number of contacts, the method overcomes the common challenge of getting trapped in low-energy states, thereby enabling the generation of configurations across a broad spectrum. We demonstrate that the resulting ensemble accurately reflects the true probability distribution of contact numbers, a critical requirement for the rigorous analysis of granular systems. Furthermore, the approach is adaptable to other systems, including those with finite friction, provided the appropriate biasing function is selected.

The Explorer-Director game is a two-player combinatorial search played on a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices. In each round, Explorer selects a vertex $v$, and Director responds by revealing a subset $S$ of the $n$-vertices such that $v$ is included in $S$. The Explorer's objective is to identify the specific target vertex chosen by Director at the outset, while Director aims to prolong the game. We demonstrate that when the Director is restricted to selecting subsets $S$ of size $k$, the number of rounds required for Explorer to locate the target is bounded by $O(n \log k)$.

This study examines the time-dependent variances and frequency-frequency correlation within the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process and standard Brownian motion, both within and outside their stationary states. We demonstrate that the variances of frequency components in the time series can be expressed through generalized expressions of the time-dependent variances associated with the mean-squared displacement. Furthermore, we find that the rate at which frequency-frequency correlation decays over time is governed by the relaxation function.

This study examines the incompressible Euler equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$ featuring a time-dependent, irrotational, bounded potential. We demonstrate that if the background irrotational flow possesses sufficient decay at infinity, one can regulate vorticity to maintain the energy of the total flow constant. This result is achieved by manipulating vorticity through boundary conditions on the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map at a specific boundary. Our proof relies on the smallness of the background irrotational flow and applies the backsteaming technique.

We introduce VIRUP, a system that enables users to explore and navigate extensive virtual reality datasets. To ensure a seamless and immersive experience, VIRUP employs a hybrid rendering approach that combines GPU-based rendering with Level of Detail (LOD) techniques. Furthermore, the system incorporates user interface elements designed to facilitate intuitive data exploration and navigation.
